basis: TCAP-associated hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; no evidence of a separate skeletal muscle or neurologic disorder.
RIPK1 immunodeficiency; intestinal inflammation 4/4 and gastritis 3/4; structural lung damage with bronchiectasis 2/4.
Glycogen metabolism disorder causing progressive myoclonic epilepsy and neurodegeneration; peripheral deposits alone do not establish organ dysfunction.
CR2-associated antibody deficiency; recurrent infections, diarrhea and splenomegaly do not establish additional direct organ damage.
APC2-associated intellectual developmental disorder with seizures; minor craniofacial and digital differences do not establish additional organ damage.
Autoinflammatory skin and intestinal disease; blepharitis 2/2 supports ocular inflammation. Otitis externa 2/2 omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Guanarito viral hemorrhagic fever with characteristic bleeding and hematologic dysfunction; common lasting damage to other organs is not established.
Inherited keratoconus causes corneal thinning and ectasia.
Malignant neoplasm arising from peripheral neural tissue in the mediastinum; thoracic location alone does not establish lung involvement.
Autoinflammation, immunodeficiency and abnormal glycogen storage; skeletal muscle amylopectinosis is characteristic and cardiomyopathy affects roughly a third or more of reported patients.
Progressive muscle disease; cataracts and cardiac conduction defects commonly exceed 50%; endocrine dysfunction affects roughly 30% or more, varying by subtype.
Umbrella disorder of epidermal cornification; extracutaneous disease varies across subtypes and associated conditions.
Cardiac/hepatic syndrome with cleft palate; sensorineural hearing loss 2/2. Variable renal and neurologic abnormalities omitted at the four-axis cap.
Defined by peripheral neuropathy and nephropathy; proteinuria 12/12 and kidney failure 11/12. Sensorineural hearing loss occurs in 4/12 (~33%).
Melanoma arising in dermal melanocytes; histologic neurotropism alone does not establish common functional nerve damage.
Umbrella disorder of glycine/serine metabolism; the broad definition does not establish common direct damage to a particular additional organ.
Inherited central movement disorder causing myoclonus and dystonia; abnormal muscle activity does not establish primary muscle disease.
Cardiac defects, cleft palate and neurodevelopmental impairment define the syndrome; digital skeletal malformations are also defining. Isolated pulmonary finding omitted at cap.
Polypoid lesion arising from the anus.
Thymic neuroendocrine carcinoma originates in the thymus, outside the listed organ axes; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish an endocrine gland disorder.
Retinal ciliopathy causes retinal degeneration; neurologic, renal and hearing abnormalities are subtype-specific rather than common across this umbrella.
Salivary gland or duct calculus; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Contiguous deletion syndrome combines Greig skeletal malformations with frequent significant developmental impairment; hypertelorism alone is not ocular damage.
Fixed drug eruption is an immune-mediated cutaneous hypersensitivity disorder; oral ulceration and stomatitis are occasional (5–29%), below threshold.
Complement-associated acquired partial lipodystrophy causes subcutaneous fat loss. Glomerulonephritis occurs in 26%, below threshold, and is separately diagnosed.
